name: hh-meanrev-micro: chop-gated band fade, low-vol regime (15m)
rationale: MECHANISM: mean reversion only pays in RANGING regimes; trend days run fades over as price keeps leaving the mean. This spec makes the REGIME the primary gate, not the trigger: fade a bb_z extreme ONLY when vol_realized sits below a fitted ceiling (compressed, mechanical oscillation), explicitly refusing to trade when realized vol is elevated (breakout/trend risk). The economic other side is the inventory-managing maker who profits fading noise around a stable mid only when there is no directional flow imbalance — grid/MM bots keep re-quoting a range until flow forces a break, so within-range reversion is a repeatable micro-oscillation they manufacture. Entry: bb_z below a fitted floor AND vol_realized below a fitted low-vol ceiling. Long-only spot; exit on bb_z reversion toward zero. DISCONFIRMER: split the sample by realized-vol quartile — if the low-vol quartile does NOT show a materially higher net Sharpe than the high-vol quartile, the regime gate adds nothing and is a fitted threshold. If performance flips sign out-of-sample when the vol cutoff is nudged 10-20%, the gate is an artifact — kill. A real regime effect is monotone in the vol rank, not a knife-edge at one value.
catalyst: band extreme faded only inside a low-realized-vol ranging regime
